name: PowerShell (Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+)
summary: Object-pipeline shell. Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe, built into Windows, PSReadLine 2.0.0) and PowerShell 7+ (pwsh, cross-platform, newer PSReadLine and PSStyle).
license: MIT (PowerShell 7); Windows PowerShell 5.1 is part of Windows
configFormat: PowerShell script ($PROFILE); line editor options via PSReadLine cmdlets
startupCostMs: Measured on Windows 11, Windows PowerShell 5.1 (single run): powershell -NoLogo -NoProfile -Command exit = 208 ms; same with a rich profile (PSReadLine 2.4 import, prompt, idle-loaded zoxide) = 531 ms. Importing modules and calling external tools in $PROFILE is where time goes; PowerShell 7 has a similar order of magnitude (not measured here).

install.notes: PowerShell 7 (pwsh). Windows PowerShell 5.1 is built in and cannot be uninstalled.

windows.notes: {ps-profile} = Windows PowerShell 5.1 profile (Documents\WindowsPowerShell\Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1), {pwsh-profile} = PowerShell 7 profile (Documents\PowerShell\Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1). Documents may be redirected by OneDrive: trust $PROFILE. Save 5.1 profiles as UTF-8 with BOM. PowerShell 7 validate: replace powershell with pwsh.

install.notes: From the Microsoft package repository (packages.microsoft.com); not in default Debian/Ubuntu repos.

linux.notes: {pwsh-profile} = ~/.config/powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1. Also installable via snap (powershell --classic) or the tarball.

prompt.notes: function prompt {}; transient prompt via a PSReadLine Enter handler.

line-editing.notes: PSReadLine. 5.1 ships 2.0.0 (no predictions); install >= 2.2 for prediction list view.
